r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped dependencies and reviewed recent changes for notification-service and related services. notification-service depends asynchronously on event-bus and synchronously on sms-vendor and push-provider. payments-api also depends on event-bus. Review of deployments over the last 7 days identified an infrastructure change on notification-service (kernel security update) on Oct 12 and an event-bus credential rotation on Oct 8, with no changes deployed on the day of the incident for these services.

findings.statement: notification-service depends on event-bus asynchronously, and on sms-vendor and push-provider synchronously.
payments-api also depends on event-bus asynchronously.
A notification-service node pool patch for a kernel security update occurred on 2026-10-12T08:19:00+00:00.
An event-bus API credential rotation occurred on 2026-10-08T15:02:00+00:00.
No code deployments or configuration changes were found for sms-vendor or push-provider in the 7 days prior to the incident.

open_questions: What specific errors or error codes are returned by sms-vendor and push-provider when calls fail intermittently?
Did the kubernetes control plane record any OOM kills, pod restarts, or scaling events for notification-service around the 13:25 onset?

r1-observability-1.summary: Notification-service experienced an error rate spike starting at 13:25 UTC, reaching over 24 percent. Logs show persistent DNS resolution failures (getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN) for both sms-vendor.example.net and fcm.push-provider.example.com beginning at 13:25:05 UTC.

findings.statement: metric:notification-service:error_rate_pct shows an anomaly onset at 2026-10-14T13:25:00+00:00, with error rates jumping from a baseline of ~0.27% to a peak of 26.58%.
notification-service logged getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN errors for fcm.push-provider.example.com starting at 2026-10-14T13:25:05+00:00 (first_id log-00531).
notification-service logged getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN errors for sms-vendor.example.net starting at 2026-10-14T13:25:10+00:00 (first_id log-00533).
metric:notification-service:rps, latency, CPU, memory, and pod restarts showed no anomalous behavior during the incident window.
The DNS resolution failures indicate that platform-level DNS or coredns resolution is likely failing for external vendors, rather than an internal resource exhaustion issue.

open_questions: Why did DNS resolution for external vendor domains start failing at 13:25 UTC?

r2-observability-1.summary: Investigation of the coredns service reveals that latency, error rate, and CPU metrics began an abnormal upward trend at 13:23 on 2026-10-14, matching closely with the onset of name resolution and timeout issues in notification-service at 13:25.

findings.statement: coredns latency_p99_ms experienced an anomaly starting at 2026-10-14T13:23:00+00:00, peaking at 2112.52 ms.
coredns error_rate_pct experienced an anomaly starting at 2026-10-14T13:23:00+00:00, peaking at 22.72%.
coredns cpu_pct experienced an anomaly starting at 2026-10-14T13:23:00+00:00, peaking at 105.92%.
coredns logged udp timeout errors trying to resolve sms-vendor.example.net starting at 2026-10-14T13:24:03+00:00.

open_questions: What caused the sudden spike in coredns CPU utilization and DNS query timeouts?

hypotheses.title: Cluster CoreDNS service degradation
hypotheses.mechanism: CoreDNS experienced internal CPU saturation (peaking at 105.92%) and query timeouts starting at 13:23 UTC, leading to UDP timeouts when attempting to resolve external vendor domains. This caused downstream getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN resolution errors in notification-service beginning at 13:25 UTC.

supporting.note: Shows coredns error rates started rising at 13:23:00 UTC, directly preceding the notification-service error spike.
Shows coredns p99 latency spiked from ~3ms to over 2112ms starting at 13:23:00 UTC.
Shows coredns CPU utilization spiked past 100% starting at 13:23:00 UTC.
Shows coredns logging UDP timeout errors resolving sms-vendor.example.net starting at 13:24:03 UTC.
Shows the exact onset of the error rate anomaly at 13:25:00 UTC, immediately following coredns degradation.
Shows persistent getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN for push-provider starting at 13:25:05 UTC.
Shows persistent getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN for sms-vendor starting at 13:25:10 UTC.
Past incident confirms prior occurrences of EAI_AGAIN errors across cluster services due to CoreDNS issues.

contradicting.note: CoreDNS overall RPS showed no major spike or anomaly, staying relatively stable around 3500 req/s.

assumptions: The CPU spike and query timeouts in CoreDNS were triggered by upstream recursive resolver latency or a burst of specific query patterns that exhausted CoreDNS worker threads.

hypotheses.title: External vendor nameserver timeouts
hypotheses.mechanism: Upstream DNS infrastructure managed by external network providers experienced intermittent routing or packet loss, causing DNS queries originating from CoreDNS to time out specifically for vendor hostnames.

supporting.note: Shows CoreDNS timing out specifically when querying UDP for sms-vendor.example.net.
Shows notification-service failing to resolve sms-vendor.example.net with EAI_AGAIN.

contradicting.note: CoreDNS CPU utilization spiked to 105.92%, indicating internal resource contention rather than simple pass-through network packet loss.
CoreDNS errors started internally at 13:23 UTC before vendor-specific queries failed.

assumptions: External recursive DNS networks or vendor authoritative nameservers suffered intermittent packet loss.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The critic's review pointed out the lack of telemetry for coredns in round 1 and the usage of an unknown service name. In round 2, coredns metrics and logs were retrieved, conclusively demonstrating that coredns itself suffered an anomaly starting at 13:23 UTC (CPU spike to 105.92%, p99 latency spike to 2112.52ms, and error rate spike to 22.72%), directly preceding notification-service's DNS failures at 13:25 UTC. H1 has been updated to cite the coredns metrics directly, replacing the old external_dns hypothesis with a valid service-based hypothesis (H2 targeting sms-vendor).

issues: The top hypothesis H1 (CoreDNS degradation) has no direct telemetry retrieved for the coredns service itself, leaving its health unverified.
